name: media_rss_sweep
what: Live RSS sweep of 8 popular Indian newspapers' section feeds -- Economic Times, Hindu, Hindu Business Line, Times of India, Livemint, Moneycontrol, Business Standard (English) + Amar Ujala (Hindi) -- filtered for investment-intent language (English + Devanagari keywords), matched against real 23-country foreign stock-market rosters (same files layer 42 uses). Full article text pulled only for roster-confirmed hits. Originally a workaround for ET/Hindu/HBL blocking Anthropic's hosted crawler/search infra outright -- runs via subprocess curl from the local machine, which is never blocked (see feedback_economic_times_blocked memory) -- kept as the standard fetch method when extended to more sources for consistency. CAVEAT on the Hindi source: company-name matching only catches names Indian financial press conventionally leaves in Latin script (Apple, Tesla, Toyota); transliterated names (e.g. एप्पल for Apple) are invisible to the shared Latin-script matcher -- partial, not full, non-English coverage. Separate CAVEAT: 'strong' fragment matches on generic industry-descriptive company names (e.g. 'Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp' vs. any article about semiconductor manufacturing in general) still slip through even after the SPAC/share-class filter -- treat every match here as a candidate for human review via its full_text field, not a confirmed lead, same as layer 44's un-reviewed MoU rows.

matches.title: We have invested $16 billion in R&D of less harmful alternatives for smokers: Philip Morris International’s Tomoko Iida
matches.full_text: Tashkent: Philip Morris International (PMI) is offering a range of less harmful alternatives for smokers and has invested USD 16 billion in research, development and commercialization of such products, Dr Tomoko Iida, Senior Director, Scientific Engagement, South Asia, Indochina, CIS and Middle East & Africa, Philip Morris International, said. We have invested 16 billion dollars in research, development and commercialization of these less harmful products,  she said, adding that  science has shown us that smoking cigarettes can cause diseases, and it became clear to everyone. She further added that this was where the company decided that it needed to transform itself, in a world where more than 1 billion smokers still exist.Speaking with at the Technovation event in the capital of Uzbekistan, she said PMI's decision to transform its business was based on scientific evidence about the health risks associated with cigarette smoking and the need to address the continued presence of smokers globally. Science has shown us that smoking cigarettes can cause diseases,  she said. We are the company who know about the smokers very well. We know about tobacco leaves, and we have equipped ourselves with the science and research,  she said. Iida said nicotine was often misunderstood and stressed that while it is addictive and not risk-free, it is not the primary cause of smoking-related diseases. Nicotine, although it's not risk-free and it's addictive, is not the main or primary cause of smoking-related diseases,  she said.She said tobacco harm reduction involved offering less harmful alternatives to adult smokers who continued to smoke. In an ideal world, if every smoker quits smoking, that is the best. But we all know that is not always the case,  Iida said.According to her, more than 60 per cent of legal-age smokers do not want to quit smoking, making alternatives an important part of the company's tobacco harm reduction approach.  If you look at countries like Sweden and Japan, we have already started to see the effect of having these alternatives on public health, and I hope we can do that in your country, in India, as well,  she said.Iida said the approach to tobacco-related issues had to take into account the different cultural, social and economic contexts of individual countries. Each country has a different cultural sensitivity, a different context when it comes to the tobacco issue,  she said.She cited Japan as an example, saying smoking prevalence there had fallen from around 20 per cent in 2014 to around 10 per cent currently. matches.title: Public sector banks' Rs 7.8 lakh core corporate loan pipeline signals capex revival
matches.full_text: Mumbai: Public sector banks have reported a combined corporate loan pipeline of about â¹7.8 lakh crore, signalling stronger credit demand as companies step up investment activity.Punjab National Bank (PNB) said it has a corporate loan pipeline of â¹1.58 lakh crore. The lender said it had sanctioned more than â¹2.5 lakh crore of corporate loans in the first half of FY27, compared with about â¹4 lakh crore in the whole of FY26.Also Read | Cash landing on you: Litigation funders bet on inheritance battles over croresCentral Bank of India has a corporate loan pipeline of â¹12,000 crore, managing director and chief executive Kalyan Kumar told ET. We have â¹7,000 crore sanctioned loans, which are to be disbursed, and another â¹5,000 crore is still under process. We have a good pipeline with a current corporate book of â¹1.18 lakh crore, which is 32% of loans,  Kumar said.Also Read | Punjab National Bank eyes Rs 6,000 crore quarterly profit after record September earningsCanara Bank has a corporate loan pipeline of about â¹47,000 crore, while Indian Bank has identified opportunities worth â¹63,000 crore. State Bank of India (SBI) accounts for the largest potential opportunity among the lenders cited. Chairman CS Setty told ET in an interview on August 28 that SBI's corporate loan prospects stood at as much as â¹5 lakh crore, supported by investment plans in renewable energy, battery storage and data centres.135034606Pool of bankable projects The investment pickup is also reflected in corporate credit growth across lenders, though the pace varies widely.RBL Bank's corporate loans grew about 58% year-on-year, while Central Bank of India's corporate credit portfolio expanded 42.05%. Canara Bank's corporate and other advances rose 17.26%, Federal Bank's corporate and investment banking portfolio expanded 17%, and HDFC Bank's corporate and other wholesale loan book grew 16.4%. Corporate capital expenditure is beginning to pick up across several sectors, including steel and cement,  said Anu Agarwal, head of corporate banking at Kotak Mahindra Bank.  Companies in the renewable energy ecosystem, particularly those manufacturing solar modules and cells, are also investing in capacity expansion. Agarwal said investment activity was largely being led by mid-sized and large companies, with opportunities also emerging for smaller suppliers.RBL Bank managing director and chief executive R Subramaniakumar said the pool of bankable corporate projects was expanding as companies regained the capacity to invest and banks had sufficient capital to fund them. Quite a substantial number of corporates are creating a capex and there is a huge opportunity building up,  Subramaniakumar said.

matches.title: Banks also count cost of insurance payout curbs
matches.full_text: Mumbai: Banks are assessing the impact of the proposed insurance commission curbs. Central Bank of India is expecting a 33% drop in bancassurance fees while Canara Bank is estimating a â¹145-crore hit to fee income, according to top executives of these lenders.Axis Bank, meanwhile, is planning to offset the potential loss through higher sales volumes, changes in product mix and alternative fee income, according to its management. HDFC Bank said it is too early to assess the impact.The changes proposed by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Irdai) to insurance commissions seek to rein in distribution costs and improve transparency in sales. For banks, which earn commissions by selling policies through their branches and other channels, lower payouts could put pressure on a key source of non-interest income.Central Bank MD and CEO Kalyan Kumar said he expects bancassurance fees to fall to â¹49 crore from â¹76 crore if the proposals take effect in their current form. The business accounts for about 8% of the bank's fee income, according to Kumar. Our Banca insurance fees are â¹76 crore or about 8% of fee income. It will come down to â¹49 crore, which means a 33% income impact as things stand,  Kumar said.The bank expects to recover the shortfall once its two new life and general insurance ventures stabilise, and through products such as credit-linked insurance, he said.Canara Bank's management said during an earnings call that it expects a â¹145-crore impact on fee income. Executives at Axis Bank, which reported a 6% YoY increase in fee income to â¹6,381 crore in the September quarter, said the bank is preparing for the changes but has not quantified its exposure. We've done some of the work on our side in terms of what the potential impact could be and how we could mitigate, through a combination of volume, product mix, etc.,  Axis Bank's management said during an earnings call.The lender said it expects six to nine months to prepare for the changes and will seek to generate additional fee income from other businesses to cushion the impact.Axis Bank is also betting that lower insurance prices could spur demand, which would allow higher volumes to compensate for reduced commissions, as was seen in higher insurance sales following the reduction in GST on premiums.

The company aims to add about 1 GW annually as it seeks to move India into its group of leading markets. CEO Catherine MacGregor tells Kalpana Pathak how Engie plans to scale up while protecting returns, navigate grid and land constraints, and build its presence in the country's energy transition. Our focus right now is to develop new renewable energy projects as well as storage. Today, we have a portfolio of around 2 GW, including projects under construction and in operation, and we are looking to increase that to 7 GW by 2030. This would represent roughly 3 billion in new investment. We, therefore, need to add around 1 GW on average every year.Also Read: India sets zero sugar diversion for ethanol in 2026/27 tenderHow will you fund the proposed 3 billion investment?This could be a combination of debt and equity, which is being worked out right now. We have also applied to establish a treasury operation at GIFT City in Gujarat. This mechanism would help facilitate the financing of our projects.How do you plan to add around 1 GW annually in an increasingly competitive market?We are very focused on execution and certainty of delivery. It is a competitive market, so we want to protect returns. We are always open to inorganic opportunities as well. At the same time, we are building our execution capabilities across engineering, construction, operations and maintenance, including in-house capabilities. We believe this is the best way to create value. By managing projects through their entire lifecycle, we can learn from execution and operations and feed those learnings back into engineering and development. matches.title: GMR Aero Technic, Logic Air ink MoU to team up in aircraft modification, engineering capabilities
matches.full_text: GMR Aero Technic, an aircraft maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) company, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Canada-based Corporation Logic Air Inc. to collaborate on aircraft modification, engineering, certification, and obsolescence solutions for customers in India and international markets. The collaboration will focus on delivering turnkey aircraft modification solutions that can be seamlessly incorporated during planned maintenance events, aircraft redelivery programs, and transition checks. Initial areas of collaboration include Boeing 737NG navigation and operational upgrades; ATR and Dash 8 engine indication modernisation; cabin electrical and structural modifications; additional Dash 8 Q400 modifications; freighter conversion and aircraft transition support; component obsolescence and on-wing support; and training and international market development. The partnership will also explore validating, adapting, and implementing eligible Logic Air STCs and modification data for Indian and international operators, with a particular emphasis on opportunities across the Middle East and Asia-Pacific. “By combining Logic Air’s aircraft modification, engineering and certification expertise with GMR Aero Technic’s MRO infrastructure and execution capabilities, we aim to offer integrated solutions that can be delivered efficiently alongside maintenance and transition programs,’’ Ashok Gopinath, President & Accountable Manager, GMR Aero Technic, said in a release. Prashanth Rajanna, Executive Director of Strategy & Global Business Development, Logic Air Inc., said: ``This collaboration also creates a strategic platform for Canadian aerospace engineering and innovation to support the rapidly growing aviation markets in India, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.” Published on  October 16, 2026

matches.title: Stock market outlook: Geopolitical cues, earnings, FIIs to keep Dalal Street busy
matches.full_text: Stock markets are likely to track quarterly earnings, crude oil prices, foreign investor activity and developments in the Middle East in the holiday-shortened week ahead. Rupee's movement against the US dollar will also be on investors' radar, analysts said.Indian markets have risen for two consecutive weeks, supported by a strong rally in IT stocks. However, it remains to be seen whether the gains will continue, with high crude oil prices, geopolitical uncertainty, global bond market movements and uneven market breadth keeping investors cautious."Investors are likely to focus on whether the recent rally broadens beyond IT stocks and whether the benchmark indices can sustain their gains above immediate resistance levels," Ponmudi R, CEO - Enrich Money, told PTI.Stock markets will remain closed on Tuesday for Dussehra.Bank results put financial stocks in the spotlightInvestors will begin the week with the September-quarter results of HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Axis Bank in focus. The three lenders reported higher profits, although the extent of growth varied.HDFC Bank, India's largest private sector lender, recorded a 5.55 per cent rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 20,700 crore. It pointed out that the impact on treasury operations had restricted profit growth.ICICI Bank reported consolidated net profit of Rs 16,333.18 crore, an increase of 22.28 per cent from Rs 13,357.06 crore in the corresponding quarter a year ago.Axis Bank's net profit rose 39.4 per cent to Rs 7,704.67 crore in the second quarter of 2026-27, helped by higher core income and improved asset quality.The earnings calendar will remain active through the week, with Bajaj Finance, UltraTech Cement, Hindustan Zinc, Union Bank of India, IREDA, Infosys, Coforge, Crisil and Swiggy scheduled to announce their results."Banking stocks will be in focus following the weekend results from HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Axis Bank. With the Q2 FY27 earnings season gathering pace, stock and sector-specific action is likely to continue, with Bajaj Finance, UltraTech Cement, Hindustan Zinc, Union Bank of India, IREDA, Infosys, Coforge, Crisil and Swiggy among the companies scheduled to report results this week," Siddhartha Khemka - head of research, Wealth Management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd, said.Global developments and foreign flows under watchThe outlook for domestic equities will also depend on movements in international markets. US Treasury yields, crude oil prices and developments in the Middle East are among the factors expected to influence trading.Their implications for imported inflation, rupee and corporate profitability will remain important considerations. Foreign institutional investor activity and rupee-dollar trend will also be closely monitored to determine whether the recent market recovery can be sustained."On the global front, movements in US Treasury yields, crude oil prices and geopolitical developments will remain important market drivers, given their implications

matches.title: Accenture weighs $1.5 billion sale of Greater China operations amid AI shift, hires JPMorgan for review: Report
matches.full_text:
Accenture is reportedly considering selling its Greater China business in a deal that could value the operations at up to $1.5 billion.According to a Financial Times report, the potential divestment is part of the company's broader effort to sharpen its strategic focus amid growing uncertainty about how artificial intelligence (AI) will reshape the industry.Strategic review and potential buyersAccenture has enlisted JPMorgan to explore options for the unit, which encompasses mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, after receiving unsolicited interest over the past year, FT reported.Private equity firms and a select group of strategic buyers are expected to evaluate a potential acquisition.The report suggested that Accenture might retain a significant minority stake to ensure continuity for its clients. However, the review process may not necessarily culminate in a transaction.Both Accenture and JPMorgan have declined to comment on the matter.AI debate and consulting's futureThe strategic review comes at a time when Accenture is re-evaluating its resource allocation. Investors are currently debating the long-term impact of AI on the consulting sector.While the company anticipates that businesses will ramp up spending on AI implementation services, sceptics caution that increased automation could diminish the demand for traditional consulting and outsourced functions.A potential sale could free up capital for Accenture to fund acquisitions that bolster its AI capabilities, invest in more competitive client pricing, and boost shareholder returns through dividends and share buybacks, FT said.Regulatory constraints in ChinaOperations in China have become increasingly complex due to regulatory hurdles, according to FT.Tighter data security rules governing sensitive information have forced several Western professional services firms to downsize their local presence and segregate their technology systems, significantly restricting the potential for cross-border integration.Financial performance and outlook
Accenture operates in over 120 territories and reported global revenue of $74.2 billion for the financial year ended in August. Its broader Asia-Pacific operations contributed approximately $10 billion in revenue last year.

matches.title: Japanese Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation leases 50,000 sq ft office space in Mumbai's BKC for  ₹189 crore
matches.full_text:
Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation (SMBC) has leased nearly 50,000 sq ft of premium office space in Mumbaiâs Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC) from Goisu Realty Private Limited, the Indian real estate arm of Japanâs Sumitomo Realty and Development Co. Ltd.
The space was leased for a five-year tenure at a total rent of  â¹189 crore, according to property registration documents accessed by Propstack, as reported by Hindustan Times (HT).
The fresh lease, dated 6 October 2026, covers 49,820 sq ft on a higher floor of Sumitomo C65, a commercial tower in BKC. The rental agreement is priced at  â¹694 per sq ft per month, translating to a starting monthly rent of approximately  â¹3.46 crore.At this rate, the annual rental outgo will stand at about  â¹41.5 crore before any escalation.The contract includes a clause for a 15 per cent rent increase every three years and requires a security deposit of  â¹35.115 crore. Additionally, the agreement includes a nine-month rent-free period, with rent payments scheduled to commence in June 2027.Sumitomo's growing footprint in IndiaGoisu Realty develops commercial office spaces in Mumbai as part of Sumitomo Realty and Development's broader expansion strategy in India. The Sumitomo C65 project in BKC aligns with the Japanese group's long-term model of office development, leasing, and management.This is not the developer's first major transaction in the district. In 2025, US-based financial services giant JP Morgan Private Limited pre-leased 1.16 lakh sq ft in another commercial tower developed by Goisu Realty in BKC.According to Propstack documents, that transaction commanded a monthly rent of  â¹6.91 crore.BKC: India's premier commercial hub
BKC remains India's most expensive and sought-after commercial district. The area houses several key government and regulatory offices, including the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the Income Tax Department, the Goods and Services Tax (GST) office, the MMRDA, and the Family Court.
The district is also home to the US consulate, the Jio Convention Centre, and luxury hospitality chains such as Sofitel and Trident.
Prominent multinational and domestic corporations operating out of BKC include Apple, Google, Amazon, Netflix, Meta (Facebook), Tesla, Jio, the National Stock Exchange, Standard Chartered Bank, Pfizer, Blackstone, CISCO, and Spotify.
